beliefs: f is well approximated by a straight line with slope ~4.71 and intercept ~3.92 across the whole range [E11, E1, E2]
There is a small smooth S-shaped correction near zero: negative on the negative side, positive on the positive side, decaying to zero by |x|~2 [E16, E12, E10]

The correction is NOT a tanh of width ~1; it is much narrower — the data show a nearly linear ramp through zero with slope ~5.4 locally, and the deviation from the global line is roughly ±0.5 at |x|~0.5 and ~0 by |x|~1.5 [E16, E15, E14]
The near-zero region has a slightly steeper local slope (~5.4) than the far-field slope (~4.71), suggesting a small localized bump/ramp rather than a shelf [E16, E15, E14, E13]
The exact functional form of the near-zero correction is still not pinned down; a narrow Gaussian-derivative-like bump centered at 0 fits the observed pattern best so far [E16]?
notes: E16 shows the correction is much narrower than tanh(x/0.9): deviations are ~0.5 at |x|=0.5 and near zero by |x|=1.5, with local slope ~5.4 near zero. Replaced the tanh correction with a narrow Gaussian-derivative bump to match this width and sign pattern.
